meta.description: Watches any number of pages for newly published content — academic calendar, exam results, schedules, announcements. Everything is configured in ONE node: 'Watch list'. The scan is a fetch plus a line-level diff, so a poll that finds nothing costs zero tokens; SPEDA is triggered only for the pages that actually changed. Safe to activate with an empty list: it simply does nothing until you add a page.

nodes.name: Every 30 minutes
nodes.notes:
Offset minutes (7 and 37) rather than 0/30 on purpose: university sites are at their most fragile exactly on the hour, when every other scraper in the country hits them.

Every page in the watch list is checked on this one schedule. For a result page you are actively waiting on, */5 is fine — scanning stays free either way; a tighter cadence only costs politeness to the site.

nodes.name: Watch list
nodes.notes:
⚙️ EDIT HERE — this is the whole configuration surface. One { … } block per page, in the WATCHES array at the top. The comment block above it documents every field.

Each entry becomes one item, and every node downstream runs once per item, so watching ten pages needs no other change.

Safe to leave empty: no items means the run ends here, green, having done nothing.

nodes.name: Igor: scan pages
nodes.notes:
THE CHEAP HALF — runs once per page in the watch list, and takes all its settings from there. Nothing to edit here.

Igor fetches each page, strips it to visible text (links kept as 'text [href]', so a newly posted PDF arrives with its URL) and diffs it against the last snapshot SPEDA was actually told about. The FIRST scan of a new watch_id returns 'baseline' and reports nothing — otherwise the entire page would count as new.

neverError: one dead site must not fail the run and take the other pages down with it. The gate inspects each response instead.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.notes:
The cost boundary — everything downstream spends money, everything upstream does not. Pages that did not change are dropped here, and on a normal run that is all of them, so the branch stops with no items.

store.broken holds one flag PER watch_id in the workflow's static data, so a broken site warns once, not every 30 minutes, and one broken site does not mute the others.

pairedItem is set explicitly so the ack node further down can find its own page's fingerprint.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ ({ "payload": { "type": "watchdog", "event": "page_published", "job": "web_publish_watch", "automation": "Web publish watch — " + $json.watch_id, "source": "web", "watch_id": $json.watch_id, "url": $json.url, "page_title": $json.title, "added": $json.added, "added_count": $json.added_count, "removed_count": $json.removed_count, "intent": $json.alert ? ("Your web watch can no longer read " + $json.url + " (" + $json.detail + "). Tell the owner in one short line that this watch is blind and what looks wrong. Do not call any tool.") : "Something new was published on a page the owner is watching. The exact new lines are ALREADY in `added` in this payload — do NOT fetch the page again, you have the change. Write the owner one short push in their language: what appeared, and the date, deadline or link that matters. Links come through as 'text [url]' — quote the url when there is one. If the new lines are only cosmetic (a reworded menu item, a moved heading), say plainly that nothing important changed rather than inventing significance." }, "output_mode": "push" }) }}

nodes.name: Igor: trigger agent
nodes.notes:
THE EXPENSIVE HALF — one agentic turn per changed page, reached only on a real publication. The agent is per-watch (the `agent` field in the watch list), so the URL is an expression; nothing to edit here.

The new lines travel in the payload and the intent says so, so the agent does not spend a second round trip re-fetching a page Igor already read.

No neverError, deliberately: a failure must kill the branch BEFORE the ack node, leaving the snapshot uncommitted so the next poll reports the same publication again. Retries cover the 503 the trigger endpoint returns when the turn registry is at capacity.

nodes.name: Igor: ack snapshot
nodes.notes:
Commits each scanned page as its new baseline, so the next scan diffs against what the agent was actually told about and never re-reports it. This is what stops the same announcement pushing every 30 minutes.

$('Gate').item — not .first() — so with several pages changing at once each ack commits ITS OWN page.

Deliberately AFTER the trigger: committing first would lose a publication whenever the notify call failed. The cost of this ordering is a possible duplicate push if the trigger succeeds and this call fails; that is the right trade for 'never miss the exam results'.

Returns 'stale' and commits nothing if the page changed again in between — the next poll then reports both changes together. On the blind-watch alert path the fingerprint is empty and this is a no-op.
